# Frayme SDK

> Frayme is the last-mile generative-UI layer for agents: POST a natural-language prompt to api.frayme.ai/v1/compose and get back a validated json-render UI spec, streamed as typed SSE. The SDK is three MIT npm packages: @frayme/api (typed client, agent tools, server proxy handler), @frayme/catalog (the 189-component vocabulary + spec validation), and @frayme/runtime (React renderer + Vercel AI SDK and AG-UI transport adapters).

Key facts for integrating:
- Install: `npm i @frayme/api @frayme/runtime`. On the server, use `new Frayme({apiKey})`. In the browser, use keyless proxy mode, `new Frayme({apiKey: null, baseURL: '/api/frayme'})`, and never put fr_live_ keys in a browser. `createFraymeHandler({ authorize })` from '@frayme/api/server' is the ready-made proxy route. Mount it in a catch-all route under the base URL (app/api/frayme/[...path]/route.ts), since the client posts to `<baseURL>/v1/compose`.
- Streaming events: compose.started → op×N (live, provisional) → [compose.restarted ⇒ DISCARD rendered state] → compose.completed (final, validated) | error (typed FraymeError, retryable with idempotent replay).
- Vercel AI SDK 6 agents: `tools: { ...yourTools, ...fraymeTools({ messages }) }` with `fraymeTools` from '@frayme/api/ai-sdk' (optional peer `ai`). This gives the agent frayme_compose and frayme_action, plus lookup_intent and query_source when you pass `intents` and `sources`. The screen streams to the UI as preliminary tool outputs, and the model sees only { generation_id, status, operation_count }. The model edits an earlier screen with `edit_of: <generation_id>`, not prior_spec, and screens are read only from Frayme's own finished tool outputs.
- AI SDK route rules: create the tools per request, pass the UI messages exactly as posted (metadata included), and always call `convertToModelMessages(messages, { tools })`. Without `{ tools }`, the full spec reaches the model.
- One compose per turn: a second call returns ONE_COMPOSE_PER_TURN. Only a retryable failure frees the turn (`composeErrorRetryable` from '@frayme/api/agent': a 400 or 422, a 5xx, or no status). A bad key, a plan limit, a rate limit, CLIENT_ERROR or an abort keep it.
- Refusals come back with `refused: true`, and the UI draws nothing for them. NO_PRESS, PRESS_MISMATCH, PRESS_INVALID and UNKNOWN_SCREEN are retryable; ONE_COMPOSE_PER_TURN is not. The model can't write a press, a screen or a prior_spec; the server validates everything the client sends.
- AI SDK client: for each message part, `const frayme = fraymePart(part, message)` (from '@frayme/runtime/ai-sdk'). When it's set, render `<FraymeResult {...frayme} interactive={!busy} onPress={(e) => sendMessage(pressMessage(e))}/>` (from '@frayme/runtime/react'), with `status` from useChat, so a press never starts a second request while the agent is answering. The live snapshot takes typed input but no presses. fraymePart returns null for refused outputs and for errors the model already retried in the same message. pressMessage sends the full event in metadata.frayme, and its text ends with a `frayme_action {...}` line that the agent forwards.
- Other frameworks: `import { createComposeTool, createActionTool, composeToolDefinition, anthropicToolDefinitions } from '@frayme/api/tools'`. The input schemas are Zod v4 / Standard Schema. Wiring by framework:
  - Mastra: `createTool({ id: compose.name, ...compose })`.
  - LangChain.js: `tool(execute, { schema })`.
  - Vercel AI SDK by hand: `tool({ ...compose })`.
  - OpenAI Agents JS: `tool()` rejects these Zod schemas, so pass the plain JSON Schema from `anthropicToolDefinitions()` as `parameters`, with `strict: false`.
  - The framework-neutral core (intents, sources, composeOutputs, press helpers) is '@frayme/api/agent'.
- frayme_action input: the press event verbatim (action, event, params, state, element_id, generation_id), plus `prompt`, `data`, `actions` and `signals` for the next screen. createActionTool sends the last four as top-level request fields.
- Render: `<FraymeRenderer spec={spec} onDynamicAction={...}/>` from '@frayme/runtime/react' + import '@frayme/runtime/styles.css'. Most interactions (state, tabs, typing) resolve locally with zero round-trip; spec-bound named actions reach onDynamicAction.
- Chatless screens: `<FraymeProvider endpoint="/api/frayme"><FraymeScreen prompt="..." data={...} actions={[...]} onAction={(event, screen) => screen.continue(event)}/></FraymeProvider>` (from '@frayme/runtime/react'). The props are the request, and the handle has edit, continue, retry and abort. For a custom layout, use the `useFraymeScreen()` hook.
- Theming: every `theme` prop takes a ThemeTokens set or a { light, dark } pair, and `scheme` is 'light' | 'dark' | 'system'. The helpers are useColorScheme (react) and resolveTheme / isThemePair (root). ThemeTokens includes `accent`.
- Hand-built AI SDK data parts: the server bridges with composeStreamToDataParts() (from '@frayme/runtime'), and the client renders with <FraymeMessageRenderer message={message}/> (from '@frayme/runtime/ai-sdk').
- AG-UI agents (LangGraph, CrewAI, Mastra, Pydantic AI…): deliver the spec as a CUSTOM 'frayme:spec' event, and on the client use useFraymeAgUiSpec() + <FraymeAgUiRenderer/> (from '@frayme/runtime/ag-ui'). createAgUiActionForwarder hands each press back as a { name: 'frayme:action', value: event } payload, which you pass to the agent, for example in forwardedProps.

## Docs

- [Documentation](https://docs.frayme.ai): guides, component reference, and the full API wire contract (including the SSE event union) for non-TypeScript integrations. The guides include Chatless screens, Server handler, and Intents and sources. The SDK reference has pages for @frayme/api, @frayme/api/agent, @frayme/api/ai-sdk, @frayme/api/server, @frayme/runtime and @frayme/catalog.
- [SDK repo](https://github.com/frayme-ai/frayme-sdk): source for all three packages
- [Website](https://frayme.ai): get an API key
